sections.section_title: The Final Instruction of the Household Code -- Masters
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this passage completing the household code by commanding masters to grant justice and fairness to their slaves, grounded in the recognition that they themselves serve a heavenly Master who judges without partiality.

sections.section_title: Prayer -- Persistence, Alertness, and the Open Door
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this passage commanding the community to devote itself to persistent, watchful, thankful prayer, including intercession for Paul's gospel proclamation and for God to open a door for the word so that the mystery of Christ may be made clear.

The neutral reading finds this passage instructing the community to walk in wisdom toward outsiders, seize every opportune moment for engagement, and let their speech be gracious and seasoned with salt, adapted to each individual person.

sections.section_title: The Letter Carriers -- Tychicus and Onesimus
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this passage introducing the two men sent to carry the letter and deliver oral news about Paul's circumstances: Tychicus, validated as a beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow servant, and Onesimus, identified as a faithful and beloved brother who is one of their own community.

sections.section_title: Greetings from Co-Workers -- The Network of the Messiah's Body
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this passage naming six co-workers who send greetings -- three Jewish (Aristarchus, Mark, Jesus Justus) and three Gentile (Epaphras, Luke, Demas) -- mapping the relational network through which the body of the Messiah functions, with special attention to Epaphras's intense prayer that the Colossians stand perfect and fully assured in all the will of God.

sections.section_title: Instructions for the Lycus Valley Network and Archippus
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this passage directing the Colossians to greet the Laodicean community and Nympha's house-church, to share letters between the two congregations, and to charge Archippus to watch and fulfill the ministry he received in the Lord.

The neutral reading finds this passage presenting Paul's autograph greeting, his request that the community remember his imprisonment, and the spare benediction of grace that encapsulates the letter's message of God's unsupplementable gift in Christ.
